No-retraction theorem

No closed disc retracts continuously onto its boundary. This is equivalent to Brouwer fixed-point theorem by the standard ray construction and the antipodal map.

Metric space

Words: 1k Articles: 35
Topological analysis OurBigBook.com
A metric space is a set equipped with a nonnegative symmetric distance satisfying definiteness and the triangle inequality.

Convergence in a metric space (xn​→x)

Words: 24
Metric space OurBigBook.com
A sequence (xn​) converges to x in a metric space when d(xn​,x)→0, equivalently when every neighbourhood of x contains all sufficiently late terms.

Sequential characterization of continuity in metric spaces

Words: 46
Metric space OurBigBook.com
A map between metric spaces is continuous exactly when xn​→x always implies f(xn​)→f(x). If an inverse image of an open set were not open, points outside it could be chosen within distance 1/n of a point inside it, proving the converse by contradiction.

Sequential compactness of a compact metric space

Words: 21
Metric space OurBigBook.com
Every sequence in a compact metric space has a convergent subsequence. Conversely, sequential compactness and compactness are equivalent for metric spaces.

Normality of every metric space

Words: 39
Metric space OurBigBook.com
Every metric space is normal. For disjoint closed sets A,B, the function
x⟼d(x,A)+d(x,B)d(x,A)​
(1)
is continuous, equals zero on A, and equals one on B; inverse images of disjoint neighbourhoods of zero and one separate the sets.

Bounded-continuous-function characterization of compact metric spaces

Words: 46
Metric space OurBigBook.com
A metric space X is compact exactly when every continuous function X→R is bounded. For the converse, a noncompact metric space contains a closed discrete sequence; the unbounded function assigning its nth point the value n extends to X by the Tietze extension theorem.

Every complete metric space is a Baire space: every countable intersection of open dense subsets is dense. Equivalently, no nonempty open subset is a countable union of nowhere-dense subsets.
To prove the dense-intersection form, let V be nonempty and open and let G1​,G2​,… be open dense sets. Successively choose closed balls

(4)

Isolated points in a countable complete metric space
Words: 85
Baire category theorem OurBigBook.com
Every nonempty countable complete metric space has an isolated point. Otherwise it is the countable union of its singleton subsets, each of which is nowhere dense, contradicting the Baire category theorem.
If such a space has infinitely many points, it has infinitely many isolated points. Indeed, after deleting any finite collection of isolated points, the remaining set is closed, complete, countable, and nonempty. It therefore has a point isolated in the remaining space; because the deleted set is finite, that point is also isolated in the original space.

A subset A of a topological space is nowhere dense when the interior of its closure is empty. Equivalently, every nonempty open set contains a nonempty open subset disjoint from A.
Meagre set

Baire category theorem OurBigBook.com
A meagre, or first-category, set is a countable union of nowhere dense sets.
Generic nowhere-monotone continuous function
Words: 72
Baire category theorem OurBigBook.com
In C([0,1]) with the uniform norm, the continuous functions that are monotone on some interval of positive length form a meagre set. Indeed, it is enough to use intervals with rational endpoints. For each such interval, the nondecreasing and nonincreasing functions form closed sets with empty interior: a sufficiently small local triangular perturbation breaks the relevant inequality. The Baire category theorem therefore shows that a dense set of continuous functions is monotone on no nontrivial interval.
Smooth function with a pointwise vanishing derivative
Words: 209
Baire category theorem OurBigBook.com
Let f∈C∞(R) and suppose that for every x there is an n=n(x)≥0 such that f(n)(x)=0. Then f is a polynomial.
Set Sn​={x:f(n)(x)=0} and En​=intSn​. The sets Sn​ are closed, En​⊂En+1​, and Baire's theorem on each interval shows that Ω=⋃n​En​ is dense. On every connected component of Ω, compactness and the increasing cover by the En​ show that one derivative vanishes locally with a uniform finite order, so f agrees there with one polynomial.
If F=R∖Ω were nonempty, it would be closed and have no isolated points: polynomial pieces on both sides of an isolated point would have matching derivatives of every order and hence join into one polynomial piece. Applying Baire's theorem to the cover F=⋃n​(F∩Sn​) gives an interval U and an index k for which F∩U is nonempty and contained in Sk​. Because F has no isolated points, difference quotients show that every derivative of order at least k vanishes on F∩U. Each polynomial component of Ω meeting U has an endpoint in F∩U, so its degree is less than k. Thus f(k)=0 throughout U, contradicting F∩U=∅. Hence Ω=R, and its sole connected component carries one polynomial.

(455)
Bounds ∣f′∣≥δ and ∣f′′∣≤M make ∣g′∣<1 on a sufficiently small closed interval around r. The contraction mapping theorem then gives the unique local fixed point.

Uniform approximation

Words: 61 Articles: 2
Analysis OurBigBook.com
Uniform approximation minimizes the supremum norm of the difference between a target function and an approximant.

Best uniform approximation

Words: 23
Uniform approximation OurBigBook.com
Given a family A of approximating functions, a best uniform approximation to f is an element p∈A satisfying
∥f−p∥∞​=infq∈A​∥f−q∥∞​.

Chebyshev alternation theorem

Words: 25
Uniform approximation OurBigBook.com
A degree-at-most-m polynomial is a best uniform approximation precisely when its error attains alternating extrema of equal magnitude at at least m+2 ordered points.
